name: Pakistan

demographics.notes: 5th most populous country in the world with a vast youth demographic (over 60% under age 30); rapid urbanization placing severe pressure on urban water and power systems.

economy.notes: South Asia's second-largest economy centered around the fertile Indus River agricultural plain and a large textile industrial sector; actively developing the $62 billion China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) to serve as a regional trade gateway; frequently operates under IMF stabilization programs.
major_exports: Textiles, knitwear, and cotton apparel (>55% of export earnings)
Basmati rice and agricultural food grains
Surgical instruments and specialized medical implements
Defense systems (JF-17 Thunder fighter jets, Super Mushshak trainers)
major_imports: Petroleum crude, diesel, and motor spirit
Industrial machinery, electrical components, and steel
Edible oils (palm oil from Malaysia and Indonesia)

military.defence_spending_pct_gdp_source: World Bank WDI (MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS), 2024 data, extracted from user-provided dataset (file last updated 2026-02-24)
military.arms_exports_source: World Bank WDI (MS.MIL.XPRT.KD), constant USD, from user-provided dataset
key_equipment_or_doctrines: Full Spectrum Nuclear Deterrence (FSD): Designed to deter conventional and sub-conventional Indian military operations across all escalation ladders
JF-17 Thunder Block III 4.5-generation multirole combat aircraft co-produced with China (PAC Kamra & Chengdu)
J-10CE 'Vigorous Dragon' multirole fighters and F-16 Fighting Falcon squadrons
Heavy Armor: VT-4 Main Battle Tanks, Al-Khalid I tanks, and Type 054A/P Tughril-class guided-missile frigates
Hangor-class (Type 039B derivative) air-independent propulsion (AIP) submarines under construction with China
Multi-layered Air Defence: HQ-9/P long-range and HQ-16FE medium-range SAM systems

primary_sources: Natural gas (35% - domestic Sui reserves declining, offset by LNG imports)
Hydropower (28% - Tarbela, Mangla, and ongoing Dasu/Diamer-Bhasha dams)
Coal (10% - Thar lignite mining alongside imported coal)
Nuclear power (5% - Chashma and Karachi K-2/K-3 plants built with China CNNC)
energy.note: High reliance on imported fossil fuels (crude oil and LNG) generating balance-of-payments vulnerability; power sector burdened by chronic circular debt.

major_ports: Port of Karachi (Oldest and highest-volume commercial maritime gateway handling >60% of national cargo)
Port Muhammad Bin Qasim (Industrial and deepwater energy terminal handling LNG, coal, and bulk liquids)
Port of Gwadar (CPEC flagship deepwater warm-water port in Balochistan, commanding the mouth of the Persian Gulf ~400 km east of Hormuz)
infrastructure.energy_grid_resilience: National electric grid managed by the National Transmission & Despatch Company (NTDC); faces transmission bottleneck challenges between southern power plants and northern load centers.
infrastructure.digital_infrastructure: Multiple subsea fiber cable landings at Karachi and Gwadar (PEACE Cable, SEA-ME-WE series, AAE-1); strategic overland fiber optic line linking Pakistan to China through the Khunjerab Pass.

top_partners: China (largest source of imports, capital goods, defense hardware, and infrastructure loans)
United States (largest single export destination, particularly for textiles and apparel)
United Arab Emirates (key energy supplier, source of remittances, and financial rollover partner)
Saudi Arabia (vital crude oil supplier, source of central bank deposit support, and home to 2.5M Pakistani workers)
European Union / Germany (beneficiary of EU GSP+ preferential trade access for textile exports)
chokepoint_exposure: Strait of Hormuz (over 85% of crude oil and LNG imports originate in Persian Gulf states)
Arabian Sea coastal approaches (vulnerable to naval interdiction or blockade during high-intensity conflict with India)
Khunjerab Pass / Karakoram Highway (sole direct overland corridor connecting Pakistan with China, subject to winter closures and high-altitude terrain)

core_competencies: Indigenized nuclear fuel cycle, uranium enrichment, and plutonium production for strategic weapons
Advanced ballistic and cruise missile design and manufacturing (Solid-fuel Shaheen series, Babur cruise missiles, Ra'ad ALCM)
Aviation co-production and maintenance (Pakistan Aeronautical Complex [PAC] Kamra)
Software services, freelance digital talent, and IT business process outsourcing
tech_vulnerabilities: Heavy reliance on Chinese defense OEMs for avionics, radars, engines (WS-13/RD-93), and missile seeker technology
Underdeveloped domestic semiconductor fabrication and precision electronics manufacturing base
Limited capital expenditure on commercial research and development

land_borders: India (3320 km including the Line of Control [LoC] and Working Boundary)
Afghanistan (2670 km along the disputed Durand Line)
China (596 km through the Karakoram Range)
strategic_chokepoints_adjacent: Arabian Sea / Gulf of Oman littoral
Approaches to the Strait of Hormuz
Karakoram Highway (Khunjerab Pass at 4,693 m altitude)

politics.executive: Prime Minister is head of government holding executive power, elected by the National Assembly; President is ceremonial head of state.
politics.legislature: Bicameral Parliament (Majlis-e-Shoora) comprising the directly elected National Assembly (336 seats) and the Senate (100 seats representing the four provinces).
politics.judiciary: Supreme Court of Pakistan with constitutional jurisdiction, provincial High Courts, and Federal Shariat Court.

nuclear.delivery_systems: Operational nuclear triad: road-mobile solid-fuel MRBMs (Shaheen-III range ~2,750 km, Shaheen-II, Ghauri), short-range battlefield systems (Nasr/Hatf-IX), dual-capable combat aircraft (Mirage III/V, F-16s), and submarine-launched cruise missiles (Babur-3 on Agosta 90B and Hangor-class submarines).
nuclear.notes: Estimated 170 nuclear warheads (SIPRI 2024). Governed under the National Command Authority (NCA) chaired by the Prime Minister with the Strategic Plans Division (SPD) maintaining custody. Pakistan maintains a first-use doctrine predicated on conventional military asymmetry with India.

strategic_priorities: Maintaining credible Full Spectrum Deterrence against India across conventional and nuclear domains
Preserving and deepening the 'all-weather strategic cooperative partnership' with China and securing CPEC transit corridors
Securing the western border with Afghanistan, countering cross-border militant sanctuaries (TTP), and managing the Afghan refugee repatriation
Achieving macroeconomic stabilization, fiscal debt sustainability, and industrial growth under IMF structural reform programs
Maintaining strategic balance and security cooperation with the United States while receiving sovereign financial rollovers from Saudi Arabia and the UAE
dependencies: Existential water dependency on the Indus Basin river system originating in Jammu & Kashmir and Tibet, governed by the fragile Indus Waters Treaty
High reliance on external sovereign financial rollovers (China, Saudi Arabia, UAE) and IMF tranches to avert foreign exchange liquidity crises
Near-total dependence on Chinese defense aerospace and naval systems for frontline military modernization
Imported energy reliance: ~75% of fossil fuels imported through Arabian Sea sea-lanes
vulnerabilities: Dual-front security exposure: Tense militarized conventional border with India along the LoC, combined with continuous cross-border kinetic friction and insurgent attacks along the 2,670 km Afghan border
Economic and fiscal fragility: Chronic fiscal deficits, high debt-servicing burdens, inflation, and periodic balance-of-payments emergencies
Acute climate catastrophe risk: Highly vulnerable to extreme monsoon floods (e.g. 2022 floods inundating one-third of the country) and glacial lake outburst floods in the Himalayas
Sub-national insurgencies: Asymmetric attacks by Baloch separatist militant groups (BLA) targeting CPEC infrastructure, Gwadar projects, and Chinese personnel
strengths: Full Spectrum Nuclear Deterrence: Proven, survivable nuclear triad that deters large-scale conventional military incursions across international borders
Geostrategic transit pivot: Physical overland bridge connecting landlocked Central Asia and western China directly to the warm-water Arabian Sea and Persian Gulf shipping lanes
Large, combat-tested armed forces: 654,000 active military personnel with extensive mountain, counter-insurgency, and desert warfare operational experience

All-Weather Strategic Alliance with China: Deep institutional defense co-development, diplomatic protection in the UN Security Council, and tens of billions in bilateral CPEC infrastructure investment
